text:
mira: Quick design review for the capacity control card — mock attached. We have min/max, a burst toggle, GPU pool picker, and an SLO slider. Need feedback on interactions + accessibility + copy. Figma: https://figma.redwood/capacity-card-iterC

jon: Range slider + numbers = useful, but current thumbs overlap when min ≈ max. If thumbs collide show a compact numeric-only view. Also worried about discoverability of burst settings. :mag: 

sam: Accessibility first: treat the number inputs as primary controls in tab order. Slider can be decorative. If we keep the slider, provide keyboard handles and aria updates. Example pattern: make inputs role="spinbutton" with aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax and live region updates.

alexa: Copy nits: change labels to be explicit. "Burst" -> "Burst capacity (short-term)". Button: "Enable burst capacity". Burst limit label -> "Burst max (GPUs)". Pool selector should show region: "GPU pool (us-west1)" when relevant.

mira: For the SLO guardrail, current mock shows an inline red banner: "Warning: Selected min may violate 99th percentile latency SLO. Recommend min ≤ 12 GPUs." Should this be inline or modal on save?

jon: Inline with a subtle icon. Add a small "Why this?" link that opens diagnostics drawer rather than a blocking modal. Modal feels too interruptive for tuning. :+1:

sam: Colour accessibility: don't rely on red alone. Show warning icon + text. Ensure contrast of banner and icon meets AA for non-text contrast. Also keyboard: make "Why this?" focusable and ensure screen reader announces the diagnostics open.

alexa: UX: For accidental min > max, avoid clamping silently. Show inline error on the offending input and an affordance to sync values, e.g., a tiny checkbox "Make min = max" or a suggested action button. Users get annoyed if we change their numbers without consent.

mira: Thoughts about cost estimates next to inputs? Mock shows a faint cost/month under each number field (estimated).

jon: I like inline cost estimates, but keep them lightweight and hideable. Might add a toggle "Show cost estimates" in a settings flyout.

sam: Keyboard increments need clear steps. Use step=1 for GPUs, allow fractional steps for vCPU-backed pools. Ensure increase/decrease buttons have aria-labels like "increase min GPUs".

mira: Burst interaction: separate toggle or inline stepper? I think toggle to enable then a small numeric input for the burst amount. Also show a tooltip: "Burst uses on-demand instances and may be preempted." Alexa, can you craft copy for the tooltip?

alexa: Sure — tooltip text: "Burst capacity allows short-term scaling beyond your reserved pool. Extra usage is billed at on-demand rates and may be preempted during high demand." Shorter for tooltip: "Short-term extra capacity. Billed at on-demand rates; may be preempted."

devex-bot: Figma comment created by mira on frame: Capacity Card — Iteration C. Link: https://figma.redwood/iter/CapacityCardC

jon: Pool picker idea: show tiny latency badge (p50/p99) on each pool row, hovercard with more metrics. That helps when the SLO guardrail flags a pool choice.

sam: For the slider, if thumbs collide, announce via SR: "Min and max are equal at X GPUs; use number inputs to adjust." Use aria-live polite.

mira: Acceptance criteria I'll add to the spec: 1) Keyboard-only can set min/max and toggle burst. 2) No silent clamping (explicit confirm or suggested action). 3) Inline guardrail banner with "Why this?" link to diagnostics. 4) Cost estimates optional and hideable. 5) Pool picker shows p50/p99 hovercard.

alexa: Final microcopy items: "Enable burst capacity", "Burst max (GPUs)", "GPU pool (region)", and banner CTA: "Open diagnostics" instead of "Why this?" if space allows.

mira: Thanks all. I'll update mocks: make numeric inputs first-class, slider visual-only when thumbs overlap, add aria attributes Sam suggested, replace copy per Alexa, inline cost mock beside inputs, and add latency badges in pool picker. Will push frames and ping for a11y sweep.

sam: Ping me after push, I'll run the sweep and test keyboard and SR announcements.

mira: Will do — thanks! :raised_hands:
